podcast.body: In 1969, Mary Clayton was called in the middle of the night to add background vocals to this Rolling Stones song, despite having never heard of the band. She famously recorded her part in her pajamas, delivering a "haunting backdrop" that became a legendary contribution to American music history. "She tells this story in the documentary twenty feet from stardom."

podcast.body: Mary Clayton performed a legendary guest vocal on this Rolling Stones track, recorded on November 2, 1969, at Sunset Sound in LA. She was called late at night by producer Jack Nitzsche while almost five months pregnant, initially refusing but persuaded by her husband. She arrived in her pajamas and rollers, was greeted by Keith Richards, and completed three takes. Her voice cracked powerfully on the word "murder," eliciting an impressed "woo" from Mick Jagger, creating one of the great guest vocals in history. "That has gone down in history as one of the great guest vocals on any record."
